solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Brief wrongly maligned at first performs well now (9)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in 'maligned' is its opening letter

blocks.note: someone performing well now IS IN FORM

annotation.surface: Someone badly spoken of at the start of their career is now doing well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is a verb here: to brief is to give someone information, so to brief wrongly is to misinform.
annotation.definitionFit: To brief is to inform; doing it wrongly gives wrong information.

entries.clue: Delivery agents turned up with obscure US composer (8)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning letters up makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
Charles Ives, the American modernist composer

annotation.surface: Couriers show up carrying the work of a little-known American composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery agents' sounds like couriers; the deliveries are babies.
annotation.definitionFit: The delivery is of babies, and those who carry it out are trained midwives.

entries.clue: Bare study in need of table, unfit? (5)

indicatorNotes.unfit: fit = ABLE, so 'table, unfit' is TABLE with ABLE taken out

blocks.note: to scan a page is to study it

annotation.surface: A room for study has no table and is not fit for use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unfit' does not describe the table; it tells you to remove the word for fit, ABLE, from it.
annotation.definitionFit: Bare here means barely enough, the sense of 'bare majority'; scant carries the same sense of meagre.

entries.clue: Defiant words from snowbound queen, eg, and princess (5,3,3)

indicatorNotes.snowbound: the following letters are bound inside the word for snow

blocks.note: névé is granular snow on a glacier
eg and say both introduce an example

annotation.surface: A queen and princess stranded by snow issue a rallying cry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snowbound' does two jobs: it names the snow and says the snow binds the other pieces inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A cry of refusal to give up, so defiant words in the plainest sense.

entries.clue: Gambling person’s pecuniary limits (2,4)

indicatorNotes.limits: the words 'person's pecuniary' form the limits that hold the answer

annotation.surface: A gambler has a spending cap.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, as punctuation always is in a hidden word.
annotation.definitionFit: 'On spec' means speculatively, taking a chance, which is a kind of gambling.

entries.clue: Not seemly, kin running amok in town (6,6)

indicatorNotes.running amok: letters running amok end up in disorder

annotation.surface: Relatives behave disgracefully on a rampage through town.
annotation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England, famous for its roundabouts.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the new town in Buckinghamshire is one instance of a town.

entries.clue: Anon book, evidently not anon, going around (2-3-2)

indicatorNotes.going around: going around something means surrounding it, so BY ANDY goes around the B

blocks.note: a work 'by Andy' is plainly not anonymous
B is the abbreviation for book

annotation.surface: An anonymous book turns out to have a named author after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anon' at the start is the old word for soon; the second 'anon' is anonymous. B sits between BY AND and Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned words for 'soon', 'in a little while'.

entries.clue: Delight with visit, providing money, finally (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally points to the last letter of money

blocks.note: to visit a place is to BE AT it
providing = if, as in 'providing you pay'

annotation.surface: A visitor is delighted, as long as the money comes through in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: BEATIFY is used here in its older sense of making someone supremely happy, not the church sense.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: to make supremely happy, from Latin beatus, blessed.

entries.clue: London venue‘s porter getting cross — and blame falling on a doctor (9,6)

blocks.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
to doctor a drink is to lace it

annotation.surface: A hotel porter gets angry when a doctor is blamed for something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a person but is the beer; 'doctor' looks like a person but is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'Ally Pally' in north London hosts concerts and darts.

entries.clue: US gadgets have no function? Game’s using one for nothing (10)

indicatorNotes.using one for nothing: I (one) is used in place of O (nothing)

blocks.note: a do is a party, a function
O is nothing; read together, 'have no function' is a DO with an O
HOCKEY'S with its O replaced by I

annotation.surface: American gizmos turn out to be useless, and a game is played with a spare player.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have no function?' gives DO + O: a function is a do, and no is O. Then HOCKEY'S swaps its O (nothing) for I (one).
annotation.definitionFit: American slang for a gizmo whose name escapes you, so a definition flagged as US usage.

entries.clue: Poor Greer, no good any longer (7)

indicatorNotes.Poor: something in poor shape is out of order
indicatorNotes.no good: 'no good' literally asks for no G: the good, G, is taken away

annotation.surface: Germaine Greer is judged to be no longer any good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Any longer' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'longer' is someone who longs.
annotation.definitionFit: A punning sense: someone who longs is, taken literally, a 'longer'.

entries.clue: Strongly recommend return of American serving in bar (3,2)

indicatorNotes.return of: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.serving in: the American is serving inside the bar, as a barman would

annotation.surface: An American who has worked behind a bar comes home and raves about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serving in bar' reads as a barman's job, and it is exactly that: the soldier is put inside.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for praising or hyping something up.

entries.clue: Initiative to support pound is a dicey affair! (6,5)

indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue, the second piece sits under the first, supporting it

blocks.note: a beetle is a heavy mallet, and to beetle is to pound with one

annotation.surface: Showing initiative to prop up the pound is a risky gamble.
annotation.walkthrough: A beetle drive is a British party game in which players throw dice to draw the parts of a beetle, so 'dicey' is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A dicey affair because the whole party is a game of throwing dice.

entries.clue: Amino acid in excess: a rich source (9)

blocks.note: a mine of information is a rich source

annotation.surface: An amino acid is found in abundance in some rich food source.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like nutrition advice; each word is doing a separate job.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the twenty amino acids that build proteins.

entries.clue: A school chum comes round for Easter (7)

indicatorNotes.comes round: the chum comes round, surrounding the other letters

blocks.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: A school friend visits for the Easter holidays.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: paschal lamb, paschal candle, things for Easter.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective for things relating to Easter, from pascha, so 'for Easter' fits a paschal lamb or candle.

entries.clue: Little people do will initially save king, sadly (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial letters of do and will
indicatorNotes.sadly: done sadly, the letters go wrong

blocks.note: the initials of do and will

annotation.surface: Small folk will try to rescue the king, but it goes badly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a fairy tale, and the answer belongs in it.
annotation.definitionFit: Folklore's small miners and smiths, the little people of fairy tales.

entries.clue: What might be cultivated verse in Latin I release (5,2)

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or tract of arable land
V is the abbreviation for verse

annotation.surface: A poet wonders what his Latin verses might grow into once he lets them go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Latin I' reads as a place for the verse, but it is a single instruction: I translated into Latin.
annotation.definitionFit: A dialect idiom for letting go of something.

entries.clue: Ways of greeting information broadcast (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: something broadcast is heard, so NEWS is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: A news bulletin says good morning to its listeners.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the NEWS part is heard; AVE is spelt as it is.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: roads, and figuratively lines of approach.

entries.clue: Bury agreement about putting up with different beliefs (19)

indicatorNotes.about: the agreement sits about, surrounding, the putting up

blocks.note: putting someone up for office is nominating them

annotation.surface: An agreement is buried because it would force people of different faiths to tolerate each other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting up with' looks like tolerating, but 'with' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for gatherings that span several Christian denominations, whose beliefs differ.

entries.clue: Character of old tree remains (3)

blocks.note: the Old English letter æ, or the rune of that name

annotation.surface: An old person's character survives in the remains of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: an old letter, a tree and remains, as in the ashes of the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses: the Old English letter æ, the tree, and the residue of burning.

entries.clue: Community links plan backing second church with a priest, primarily (6)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing a car means driving it in reverse, so the letters run the other way
indicatorNotes.primarily: take the primary, first letters of a and priest

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the first letters of a and priest

annotation.surface: A parish plan relies on a second church with a priest.
annotation.walkthrough: An ecomap is a diagram social workers use to chart a person's links to their community.
annotation.definitionFit: A social-work diagram charting a family's links to the community around it.

entries.clue: With kiss between hugs, grandmother embraces one college member (7)

indicatorNotes.between: the kiss goes between the two hugs
indicatorNotes.embraces: the letters so far embrace, surround, the one

blocks.note: O is a hug, as when signing off xoxo

annotation.surface: A grandmother hugs and kisses a grandchild who has got into a university college.
annotation.walkthrough: OXO + NAN makes OXONAN, and that whole string embraces I.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone from Oxford University, whose members belong to colleges.

entries.clue: Passed girl buried in large wordbook (6)

indicatorNotes.buried in: the girl's name is buried inside the dictionary

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary, a very large one

annotation.surface: A girl who passed her exams was always buried in a dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed' looks like it could mean died, with 'buried' to match; here it means approved.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal: to give something the OK is to pass it.

entries.clue: When speaking, limit what’s boring in pedestrian procedure (4,5)

indicatorNotes.When speaking: the word for limit is taken by how it is spoken

annotation.surface: A dull speaker drags on through a tedious procedure.
annotation.walkthrough: The kerb is the British spelling of the curb at the edge of the pavement; the kerb drill (look right, look left) was taught to British children.
annotation.definitionFit: A British road-safety routine, look right, look left, for people on foot.

entries.clue: Simple track taking very little time, note, or trouble (8)

blocks.note: N is an abbreviation for note

annotation.surface: A plain little tune that takes hardly any time or effort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Simple' means single, so 'simple track' is a one-rail line.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Simple' in its sense of single: one rail, one track.

entries.clue: Healthy way to go! (4,3,3)

blocks.note: a cry of congratulation, like 'well done!'

annotation.surface: A cheery endorsement of a healthy way to die.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Way to go' reads as a manner of death, and the exclamation mark turns it into a cheer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: healthy food, and a cheer of 'well done!'.

entries.clue: Cavorting drunkenly round a deck, getting imprisoned (5,4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.Cavorting: letters cavorting jump about into a new order

annotation.surface: A drunk capering around a ship's deck ends up in the brig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunkenly' looks like a second indicator, but it is fodder; 'round' gives the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom for locked up securely, in prison.

entries.clue: Adapting easily to UK, I work, play (2,3,4,2)

annotation.surface: An immigrant settles easily in Britain, gets a job and enjoys life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' and 'play' look like opposites; together they are the definition, a Shakespeare comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Shakespeare comedy, both a work and a play.

entries.clue: Made turn, surprisingly, that’s not fancied (8)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: the letters come out in a surprising order

annotation.surface: A racehorse nobody backed made its move at the turn, to everyone's surprise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not fancied' sounds like racing slang for an outsider; here to fancy is to imagine.
annotation.definitionFit: Past participle of 'dream': never imagined, never fancied.

entries.clue: Host poking spot on pet (6)

indicatorNotes.poking: the host pokes into the middle of the other phrase

blocks.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
spot on = to a T, exactly

annotation.surface: A host prods a spot on the family pet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot on' must be read as one phrase, TO A T, not as a spot on the pet.
annotation.definitionFit: A male cat, one kind of household pet.

entries.clue: Band turning up almost sure to meet agents (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from the bottom

annotation.surface: A pop band on the rise is nearly certain to meet some spies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests music, but a fascia is a flat band, as on a shopfront or in anatomy.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term for a flat strip, as over a shopfront, or a sheet of tissue in anatomy.

entries.clue: Result — of successful pay negotiations? (5)

blocks.note: verb: to come about as a consequence
the successful outcome of pay talks is a single increase in wages, written as two words

annotation.surface: A union asks what came of its successful wage talks.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the result of successful pay talks is a rise.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: problems arise from, i.e. result from, a cause.

entries.clue: Exaggerate in describing remaining attraction (8)

blocks.note: a draw is an attraction, as a star draws crowds

annotation.surface: Someone overstates the appeal of what is left.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'in describing': to overdraw a character is to exaggerate it in a portrait.
annotation.definitionFit: To overdo a portrait or character sketch, the drawing sense of 'draw'.

entries.clue: What goes on to madden dumbfounded hosts (8)

indicatorNotes.hosts: the words host the answer inside them

annotation.surface: Asking what is going on, enough to madden anyone left speechless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What goes on' is not 'what is happening' but what is added on at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for 'thing to be added', so something that goes on the end of a text.

entries.clue: Producer of half measure of material once brought up (2,5)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing up reads the letters from the bottom

blocks.note: the ell was an old length for cloth

annotation.surface: An old cloth measure is halved and turned up.
annotation.walkthrough: Cecil B. DeMille was the Hollywood producer and director of epics like The Ten Commandments.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Cecil B., who made Hollywood epics.

entries.clue: One pressed to retreat supports step by major (9,3)

blocks.note: key = major, crucial; 'by' simply places it next

annotation.surface: A soldier under pressure to fall back is backed up step by step by his major.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pressed to retreat' sounds military, but it is a key you press to move the cursor back.
annotation.definitionFit: The keyboard key that moves the cursor back one space.

entries.clue: Do some beer, maybe almost all for relations? (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: the last letter of all is dropped

blocks.note: to do someone is to con them

annotation.surface: Get some beer in, enough for all the family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like relatives; here it is marital relations, the phrase 'conjugal rights'.
annotation.definitionFit: Relating to marriage; the clue's 'relations' points to the idiom of a married couple's rights.

entries.clue: Outrageous perhaps fat cabbage containing trace of blight (11)

indicatorNotes.trace of: a trace is just the first letter

blocks.note: fat is one way of being not thin
kale is a kind of cabbage

annotation.surface: An outrageously fat cabbage turns out to have blight.
annotation.walkthrough: UNTHIN is not a dictionary word; 'perhaps' warns that fat is just one example of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Too outrageous to be considered, beyond thought.

entries.clue: Primate shot holding Polish off (5,3)

indicatorNotes.holding: the shot holds the other word inside it

blocks.note: grape is grapeshot, a cluster of small shot
to polish off food is to eat it

annotation.surface: A gunshot catches a Polish soldier off guard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality; with 'off' it is the phrase polish off.
annotation.definitionFit: The group of large primates: gorillas, chimps, orang-utans.

entries.clue: Straddling sharp double bend, lay a stop sign in Riyadh (5)

indicatorNotes.Straddling: the letters HAM A sit either side of the bend

blocks.note: a ham is an amateur, a lay person
the Z shape of a sharp double bend, as on a road sign

annotation.surface: A road sign in Saudi Arabia warns of a sharp double bend and tells drivers to stop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop sign' is not a road sign but the glottal stop mark in Arabic writing; Riyadh places it in Arabic.
annotation.definitionFit: The mark used in Arabic writing for a glottal stop.

entries.clue: Demanding a lounger’s callous! (4,2,5)

blocks.note: a hard task is a demanding one
a snail is a slow mover, a lounger

annotation.surface: A poolside sunbather complains about their hardened skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Callous' also hints at calluses on the lounger's feet, which is the surface joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom for tough and unfeeling, as a callous person is.

entries.clue: Records judges for hangings (10)

annotation.surface: Court records show judges sending people to be hanged.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is grim, courts and hangings; the hangings are wall-hangings.
annotation.definitionFit: Woven wall-hangings, so hangings in the decorative sense.

entries.clue: Statement from working cashier having bother finding drink (11)

blocks.note: a cashier at work says 'I AM ON TILL'

annotation.surface: A harassed cashier explains why a drink is needed.
annotation.walkthrough: The cashier's statement is 'I am on till', minus the I, which the clue leaves unspoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a medium-dry Spanish sherry.

entries.clue: Crossing motorway, I’m wise, following line (2,7)

indicatorNotes.Crossing: the phrase for 'I'm wise' crosses over the M

blocks.note: ONE'S SAGE: one is wise, the formal way of saying I am

annotation.surface: A driver boasts about their wisdom while pulling on to a motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: A politician on message sticks to the party line.
annotation.definitionFit: Political jargon for sticking to the party line.

entries.clue: Likes room to manoeuvre, taking left turn in boat (6,4)

indicatorNotes.to manoeuvre: letters given room to manoeuvre move about

annotation.surface: A canoeist wants space to manoeuvre before turning left.
annotation.walkthrough: An Eskimo roll is the kayaker's move of capsizing and righting in one turn.
annotation.definitionFit: The kayaker's manoeuvre of rolling right over and back up, a turn in a boat.

entries.clue: Open lock for releasing sort of collar (4-4)

indicatorNotes.for releasing: the letters are released to fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A lock is opened to free a dog's collar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Collar' fits the lock story as a restraint, but it is a knitted neckline.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the high, folded neckline of a jumper.

entries.clue: Mix, briefly, by fireside (9)

indicatorNotes.briefly: the word for the comma is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: the comma itself, spelt out as COMMA and cut short
an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

annotation.surface: A quick mix by the fire.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Mix' is part of the wordplay: COMMA, briefly, is COMM.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to blend together.

entries.clue: Be punished for holding barrister up in compartment (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: the phrase holds the barrister inside it
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, the barrister's letters go up, reading backwards

blocks.note: to cop it is to be punished
a KC is a King's Counsel, a senior barrister

annotation.surface: Someone is punished for holding a lawyer up in a train compartment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' is only a joining word; 'Be punished' alone gives COP IT, which holds CK.
annotation.definitionFit: Where the pilot sits in an aircraft, a separate compartment at the front.

entries.clue: Glaswegian goes, lifting Cockney’s hat and hood (7)

indicatorNotes.lifting: in a down clue, lifting the letters reads them upwards

blocks.note: in Scots, gang means go, so a Glaswegian 'gangs'

annotation.surface: A Glaswegian leaves, raising a Cockney's hat and pulling up his hood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like headgear to go with the hat; it is a hoodlum.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang spelling of gangster; a hood is a hoodlum.

entries.clue: Parrot quietly nestling in tree a kilometre back (6)

indicatorNotes.nestling in: the quiet letter nestles inside the tree
indicatorNotes.back: the whole is read back to front

blocks.note: P, piano, is quiet in music

annotation.surface: A parrot nests quietly in a tree a kilometre away.
annotation.walkthrough: O(P)AK + A + K gives OPAKAK, which reads back as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the flightless nocturnal parrot of New Zealand.

entries.clue: One chasing ball of wool maybe raising new jumper finally (7)

annotation.definition: One chasing ball of wool maybe raising new jumper finally

indicatorNotes.raising: in a down clue, the N is raised to a higher place in the word
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of jumper

blocks.clueFragment: One chasing ball of wool maybe
blocks.note: kittens are known for chasing balls of wool
N is new; it names the N at the end of KITTEN, which is raised to second place

annotation.surface: A kitten chases a ball of wool until it jumps on a new jumper.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a knitter works through a ball of wool to raise a new jumper.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue is the picture: someone working through a ball of wool to make a new jumper.

entries.clue: Watch outside broadcast from the right pavilion (6)

indicatorNotes.from the right: reading from the right reverses the letters

annotation.surface: A TV crew watches an outside broadcast from a pavilion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the right' reverses only OB; GAZE is read normally.
annotation.definitionFit: A small garden pavilion or summer-house.

entries.clue: Almost nothing, from Le Monde, is put in shredder (6)

indicatorNotes.Almost: the last letter of zero is dropped
indicatorNotes.put in: the French word is put inside

blocks.note: est is French for is; Le Monde is a French newspaper

annotation.surface: A French newspaper story is shredded into almost nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From Le Monde' tells you to put 'is' into French.
annotation.definitionFit: The kitchen tool that shreds the peel of citrus fruit.

entries.clue: Leaves, since informal function curtailed (3)

blocks.note: a variety of lettuce, grown for its leaves
the cosine function, written in its short form

annotation.surface: Someone leaves because a relaxed party was cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: A triple definition: a lettuce, a casual 'because', and cosine cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses: a lettuce, a casual 'because', and cosine abbreviated.

entries.clue: Russian once in charge of think tank with no on-screen broadcast (10,9)

annotation.surface: A think tank gets no airtime from the Kremlin's old leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Chernenko led the Soviet Union briefly in 1984–85, between Andropov and Gorbachev.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Soviet leader of 1984-85.

entries.clue: Marks appearing evenly on paper veil (5)

annotation.surface: Marks show up evenly on a paper veil.
annotation.walkthrough: The selection starts at 'on', not at 'paper'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plural of naevus, a birthmark or mole.

entries.clue: Recreation facility specially devised by US pal (7)

indicatorNotes.specially devised: the letters are devised into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An American friend has built a leisure centre.
annotation.walkthrough: A playbus is a bus converted into a mobile playgroup, a British community scheme.
annotation.definitionFit: A British community scheme: a bus fitted out for children's play.

entries.clue: Get to river crossing close to east Siberian city (7)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the river crosses over the letter
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of east is its last letter

blocks.note: something that gets you irks you
the Usk, a river in Wales

annotation.surface: Directions for reaching a Siberian city by crossing a river on the eastern side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get' means annoy here, not reach.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the city near Lake Baikal.

entries.clue: Short excursion on yours truly’s old boat (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: the excursion is cut short by one letter

annotation.surface: A brief outing on the writer's old boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has': the wordplay has the old boat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the ancient galley with three banks of oars.

entries.clue: You can take it from me, I do sympathise! (5)

annotation.definition: You can take it from me

blocks.clueFragment: You can take it from me
blocks.note: what you say as you hand something over
said, often twice, to comfort someone

annotation.surface: Someone offers reassurance and sympathy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take it from me' sounds like 'believe me'; it is handing something over.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: what you say handing something over, and 'there, there' in comfort.

entries.clue: Chemical analyst in role of speaker (7)

blocks.note: acting as = in the role of

annotation.surface: A chemist takes on the role of spokesperson.
annotation.walkthrough: SAYER is a rare word, but it is plainly built from say.
annotation.definitionFit: One who tests ores and metals chemically.

entries.clue: Singular credit given to detectives for measure (9)

blocks.note: the Yard, Scotland Yard, London's police detectives
buying on tick is buying on credit

annotation.surface: Detectives earn unusual praise as a measure of their success.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, so detectives stand for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A standard to judge by, originally a measuring rod a yard long.
